data.narrative:
Polar Semiconductor is a Growth-stage chip design and manufacturing company that has raised $700M+ in capital, including a 2024 recapitalization led by Niobrara Capital and Prysm Capital following prior ownership by Sanken Electric and Allegro MicroSystems. The semiconductor sector includes a comp universe of 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies at various stages, though no narrow peer set exists at identical stage and valuation tier.

Given data constraints, only stage-progression analysis is applicable. Using total capital raised as a proxy base of $700M and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-to-next-stage advancement yields $840M. The public comp set (median P/S of 20.4x across three semiconductors) cannot be deployed without the target's revenue figure, which is not disclosed. Peer-median triangulation similarly fails due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting the three-company minimum threshold.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $840M, with a reasonable range between $714M and $966M, though this reflects only one methodology and carries elevated uncertainty. Key limitations include the absence of revenue data precluding revenue multiple approaches, sparse Growth-stage private chip company comps, and reliance on a single quantitative lever. Any valuation in this range should be stress-tested against actual financial performance, competitive positioning within the addressable market, and capital efficiency relative to the $700M already deployed.
